argument:
Apple's bullish case has breadth: revenue grew 16%, with double-digit growth across iPhone, Mac, Services and every geography. That diversified operating expansion is more useful than relying on the 29% EPS headline alone. Observed record quarterly operating cash flow and price above both major averages support the possibility that business strength continues to sustain investor demand.

Gross margin includes roughly two percentage points of tariff refunds and EPS includes $0.11 of benefit. These must be normalised before extending the growth rate. At a vendor trailing 38.17x, no valuation margin of safety is demonstrated, and cash flow has not been fully reconciled to debt and capex. Consolidating technicals suggest a patient quality-growth thesis rather than a fresh momentum trigger.
key_points: Growth extends across products, services and geographies.
Tariff refunds inflate observed profitability and require normalisation.
Premium valuation needs sustainable operating growth, not headline EPS extrapolation.
